_comment: uv.lock carries a self-referential entry for this project, and release-please
bumping pyproject.toml without it left the lock PERMANENTLY one version behind
(overseer-bg2.10). The first `uv run` in any fresh clone or worktree then
regenerated it and left the tree dirty with a one-line restatement nobody
authored, which every session had to notice, attribute and route around.
THE `.name.value` IN THE FILTER IS LOAD-BEARING, NOT A TYPO. release-please's
toml updater parses with a position-tracking parser that wraps every scalar as
{start, end, value}, so `@.name` is an OBJECT and `@.name=='livespec-overseer'`
never matches. The obvious-looking `$.package[?(@.name=='livespec-overseer')]
.version` was tested against this exact file and SILENTLY MATCHED NOTHING:
release-please logs 'No entries modified' at warn level and returns the content
unchanged, so a wrong path here reports success while doing nothing.
Verified by running release-please 17.10.4's GenericToml updater against this
repo's real uv.lock before this landed: exactly ONE line changes, the one
directly under `name = "livespec-overseer"`, with the line count unchanged even
for a different-length version. If you edit this entry, re-run that check --
the failure mode is silence, not an error.
The version literal is carried in `overseer/version.json`, NOT in
`overseer/version.py`, and release-please must update both this package
copy and the mirrored `.claude-plugin/overseer/version.json` copy.
`source_trees = ["overseer"]` (armed 2026-07-27) puts every `.py` here
into check-red-green-replay's product-implementation bucket, and
release-please cannot author a Red->Green pair or a green-verified leg.
A `.py` target therefore produces a release commit that FAILS the gate
and blocks the release PR — observed on PR #180, commit a54e233, which
is why this moved. Every other fleet member arms `source_trees` and
generates no `.py`; this repo was the only outlier.
`json` rather than `generic` because a bare data file has no comment
syntax to carry an `x-release-please-version` marker.
THE BYTE-IDENTICAL MIRROR OF `overseer/version.json` INSIDE THE PLUGIN
PACKAGE. `check-codex-plugin-runnable-launcher` requires every file in
`overseer/` to `cmp -s` against its `.claude-plugin/overseer/`
counterpart, so a bump that moves one and not the other leaves MASTER
RED — not the release PR, master, after the release merges.
MEASURED, NOT ANTICIPATED: release 0.16.0 (c530c70) did exactly this.
`overseer/version.json` went to 0.16.0, the mirror stayed at 0.15.0, and
`just check` failed on clean master for every session in the repo. The
mirror was introduced by e1ab505 AFTER this config was written, and
nothing tied the two together, so the gap opened at the next release
rather than at the commit that caused it.
`json` and the same jsonpath as the source entry above: the two files
must remain byte-identical, so they must be bumped by identical rules.
The nested Codex manifest mirrors its Claude sibling's name,
version and description. Keep this version entry beside the
Claude manifest entry above so release-please cannot bump the
host plugin while leaving `codex plugin list` stale.
